[[Andorra]] competed at the [[2018 Winter Olympics]] in [[Pyeongchang]], [[South Korea]], which were held from 9 to 25 February 2018. The country's participation in Pyeongchang marked its twelfth appearance at the Winter Olympics since its debut in [[1976 Winter Olympics|1976]]. The athlete delegation of the country was composed of five people: [[Mireia Gutiérrez]], [[Marc Oliveras]], and [[Joan Verdú (alpine skier)|Joan Verdú]] in alpine skiing, [[Irineu Esteve Altimiras]] in cross-country skiing, and [[Lluís Marín]] in snowboarding. They all failed to medal. Thus, Andorra has yet to win a Winter Olympic medal.

==Background==
The [[2018 Winter Olympics]] were held in [[Pyeongchang]], [[South Korea]], from 9 to 25 February 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/pyeongchang-2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250322161324/https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/pyeongchang-2018 |archive-date=22 March 2025 |access-date=17 June 2025 |work=[[International Olympic Committee]] |title=PyeongChang 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref> This edition marked the nation's twelfth appearance at the [[Winter Olympics]] since its debut at the [[1976 Winter Olympics]] in [[Innsbruck]], Austria. The nation had never won a medal at the Winter Olympics, with its best performance coming from alpine skier [[Vicky Grau]] placing 19th in the [[Alpine skiing at the 1998 Winter Olympics – Women's slalom|women's slalom]] at the [[1998 Winter Olympics]] in [[Nagano, Nagano|Nagano]], Japan.<ref name=olympedia>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/countries/AND |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250203113021/https://www.olympedia.org/countries/AND |archive-date=3 February 2025 |access-date=17 June 2025 |work=[[Olympedia]] |title=Andorra Overview |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Alpine skiing ==
{{main article|Alpine skiing at the 2018 Winter Olympics|Alpine skiing at the 2018 Winter Olympics – Qualification}}
Andorra qualified three alpine skiers.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://data.fis-ski.com/dynamic/olympic-quotas-list.html?sectorcode=al&listid=2018 |title=Alpine Skiing Quota List for Olympic Games 2018 |date=12 December 2017 |publisher=[[International Ski Federation]] |access-date=16 December 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180209194511/https://data.fis-ski.com/dynamic/olympic-quotas-list.html?sectorcode=al&listid=2018 |archive-date=9 February 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The alpine skiing events were held at the [[Yongpyong Alpine Centre]]. [[Marc Oliveras]] and [[Joan Verdú (alpine skier)|Joan Verdú]] first competed in the [[Alpine skiing at the 2018 Winter Olympics – Men's combined|men's combined]] on 13 February, placing 29th and 27th respectively. The winner of the event was [[Marcel Hirscher]] of Austria.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.olympedia.org/results/9000108 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250124002442/http://www.olympedia.org/results/9000108 |archive-date=24 January 2025 |access-date=18 June 2025 |work=[[Olympedia]] |url-status=live |title=Combined, Men }}</ref> Two days later, the two competed at the [[Alpine skiing at the 2018 Winter Olympics – Men's downhill|men's downhill]]. Oliveras did not finish his run though Verdú placed 37th. The winner of the event was [[Aksel Lund Svindal]] of Norway.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/9000100 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250119141555/https://www.olympedia.org/results/9000100 |archive-date=19 January 2025 |access-date=18 June 2025 |work=[[Olympedia]] |url-status=live |title=Downhill, Men }}</ref> 

On 15 February, [[Mireia Gutiérrez]] competed in her only event, the [[Alpine skiing at the 2018 Winter Olympics – Women's slalom|women's slalom]]. She placed 30th. The winner of the event was [[Frida Hansdotter]] of Sweden.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.olympedia.org/results/9000116 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250119002510/http://www.olympedia.org/results/9000116 |archive-date=19 January 2025 |access-date=18 June 2025 |work=[[Olympedia]] |url-status=live |title=Slalom, Women }}</ref> 

The [[Alpine skiing at the 2018 Winter Olympics – Men's super-G|men's super-G competition]] on 16 February would be the last one for Oliveras. He placed 33th while Verdú placed 28th. The winner of the event was [[Matthias Mayer]] of Austria.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.olympedia.org/results/9000101 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240813051006/http://www.olympedia.org/results/9000101 |archive-date=13 August 2024 |access-date=18 June 2025 |work=[[Olympedia]] |url-status=live |title=Super G, Men }}</ref> Verdú's last event would be the [[Alpine skiing at the 2018 Winter Olympics – Men's giant slalom|men's giant slalom]] though he did not finish in his event. The winner of the event was Hirscher.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.olympedia.org/results/9000102 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250125230516/http://www.olympedia.org/results/9000102 |archive-date=25 January 2025 |access-date=18 June 2025 |work=[[Olympedia]] |url-status=live |title=Giant Slalom, Men }}</ref>

== Cross-country skiing ==
{{main article|Cross-country skiing at the 2018 Winter Olympics|Cross-country skiing at the 2018 Winter Olympics – Qualification}}
The cross-country skiing events were held at the [[Alpensia Cross-Country Skiing Centre and Alpensia Biathlon Centre|Alpensia Cross-Country Skiing Centre]]. [[Irineu Esteve Altimiras]] first competed in the [[Cross-country skiing at the 2018 Winter Olympics – Men's 30 kilometre skiathlon|men's 30 kilometre skiathlon]] on 11 February. He finished the 15 kilometre classic of his event in a time of 43:16.5 and the 15 kilometre freestyle in 38:31.2, placing him with a total of 1:21:47.7 and 46th place. The winner of the event was [[Simen Hegstad Krüger]] of Norway.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/9000279 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250119151929/https://www.olympedia.org/results/9000279 |archive-date=19 January 2025 |access-date=18 June 2025 |work=[[Olympedia]] |url-status=live |title=30 kilometres Skiathlon, Men }}</ref>

Altimiras' next competition was the [[Cross-country skiing at the 2018 Winter Olympics – Men's 15 kilometre freestyle|men's 15 km freestyle]] on 16 February. He recorded a time of 35:40.7, placing 27th, while the winner of the event was [[Dario Cologna]] of Switzerland.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.olympedia.org/results/9000277 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241215214652/http://www.olympedia.org/results/9000277 |archive-date=15 December 2024 |access-date=18 June 2025 |work=[[Olympedia]] |url-status=live |title=15 kilometres (Freestyle), Men }}</ref> Altimiras' last competition was the [[Cross-country skiing at the 2018 Winter Olympics – Men's 50 kilometre classical|men's 50 kilometre classical]] on 24 February. He recorded a time of 2:19:08.3, placing 34th, while the winner of the event was [[Iivo Niskanen]] of Finland.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/9000278 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240523145433/https://www.olympedia.org/results/9000278 |archive-date=23 May 2024 |work=[[Olympedia]] |url-status=live |access-date=18 June 2025 |title=50 kilometres (Mass Start, Classical), Men }}</ref>

==Snowboarding==
{{main|Snowboarding at the 2018 Winter Olympics}}
The snowboarding events were held at [[Bokwang Phoenix Park]] and [[Alpensia Ski Jumping Stadium]]. [[Lluís Marín]] competed in the [[Snowboarding at the 2018 Winter Olympics – Men's snowboard cross|men's snowboard cross]] on 15 February. His first run was in a time of 1:15.47 while his second time was at 1:15.37. He did not advance further, placing him 30th. The winner of the event was [[Pierre Vaultier]] of France.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/9000909 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250123031753/https://www.olympedia.org/results/9000909 |archive-date=23 January 2025 |work=[[Olympedia]] |url-status=live |access-date=18 June 2025 |title=Cross, Men }}</ref>
